title: Contra Haeresim Nestorianam Impii Nestorianii Sermones
author: Marius Mercator
source: Translated by Claude from tmp780.tmp780.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

passages.original: Haec omnia Dominicae incarnationis sunt do- cumenta, quia neque Deus Verbum erat in monu- mento projectus. Quomodo enim resurrexit, qui uni- versitatem sustentat verbo potentiae suae, si jacebat secundum Arium? Sed neque Dei essentiam flebant mulieres, tamquam quae esset de sepulcro furto sub- ducta. Quis enim suspicetur Deitatem furacibus ma- nibus capessibilem esse? Nec iterum Jacobum Divini- tatis habuit fratrem : nec Dei Verbi mortem nos an- nuntiamus, cum Domini corpore et sanguine pascimur.
passages.english: All these are proofs of the Lord's incarnation, because God the Word was not laid out in the tomb. For how did he rise again who upholds the universe by the word of his power, if he was lying [there], according to Arius? Nor were the women weeping over the essence of God, as though it had been stolen away from the tomb. For who would suppose that the Godhead can be seized by thieving hands? Nor again did the Divinity have James as a brother; nor do we proclaim the death of God the Word when we are fed with the Lord's body and blood.

passages.original: Tu vero intende, quaeso, in haec quae dicuntur, ut contra haec ipsamque etiam escam quam hamo ap- ponentes loquuntur, defensionem paratissimam ha- beas. Scis hoc Apollinarem dicentem? Scis hanc vo- cem, id est, θεοτόχον, apud Arium plausus maximos excitare? Scis hanc quoque apud Eunomium frequen- tari? Etiam, inquis, sed non secundum illos [Baluz.. Filium], ais, hanc vocem enuntio. Laudo inficias tuas, inierim arguo te ipsum in eo quod dicis vocem hanc solam esse veritatis tenacem;
passages.english: But you, I beg, pay attention to what is said, so that against these things, and against the very bait which they put on the hook as they speak, you may have a defence fully prepared. Do you know that Apollinaris says this? Do you know that this word, that is, *theotokos* [God-bearer], wins the greatest applause with Arius? Do you know that it is also used frequently by Eunomius? "Yes," you say, "but I do not utter this word in their sense." I commend your denial; meanwhile I refute you yourself in that you say that this word alone holds fast to the truth;
passages.notes: Greek θεοτόχον is a scanning error for θεοτόκον. The bracketed "[Baluz. Filium]" is an editorial variant (Baluze reads "Filium", the Son) and is omitted from the translation. "inierim" read as "interim" (meanwhile).

passages.original: Soluta sit interim haec eis et ablata rationis speciem habens occasio, confitere utrumque, appel- lans sanctam Virginem θεοτόχον pariter et Mpwto· roxov : tu vero noli eam Θεοτόκον tantummodo appel- lare [Baluz. add. Hoc enim Apollinaris vociferatur], hoc enim Arius praedicat ac veneratur; sed adde vo- cem pariter catholicorum, quae et genitricis Dei prae- muniat intellectum, θιοτόχο? Virgo sancta, secundum unitatem, οοΟρωποτόχο?, id est, hominis genitrix se cundum parem naturam.
passages.english: Let this pretext, which has a show of reason, be removed and taken away from them for the time being. Confess both, calling the holy Virgin *theotokos* [God-bearer] and likewise *anthrōpotokos* [man-bearer]. But do not call her *theotokos* only, for Arius preaches and reveres this. Rather, add likewise the word of the catholics, which also safeguards the understanding of 'mother of God': the holy Virgin is *theotokos* according to the union, and *anthrōpotokos*, that is, mother of a man, according to the nature that is like ours.
passages.notes: The Greek words are garbled by the scan: "Mpwto· roxov" and "οοΟρωποτόχο?" are read as ἀνθρωποτόκον/ἀνθρωποτόκος (man-bearer), and "θιοτόχο?" is read as θεοτόκος. Baluze adds after "only": "For Apollinaris clamours for this"; this editorial variant is not translated.
